subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: Should OpenClaw provide a first-class private session mode, and exactly which context, persistence, telemetry, plugin, tool, channel, and provider surfaces must it exclude or may retain minimal metadata?
rationale: The requested guarantee crosses the one-user trust model, core persistence architecture, plugin and channel contracts, and security semantics; implementation cannot safely select these boundaries without maintainer intent.

options.title: Full Private Sessions
options.body: Add an additive per-session mode with program-level enforcement across every durable and private-context surface, retaining only explicitly approved minimal operational metadata.

options.title: Isolated Demo Agent
options.body: Improve a separate agent, workspace, and sandbox workflow for public demonstrations without promising zero persistence or per-session secrecy.

options.title: Require Separate Runtime
options.body: Keep the existing trust model and require separate gateways or operating-system boundaries for conversations needing strong isolation.

recommendation.title: Full Private Sessions
recommendation.body: Add an additive per-session mode with program-level enforcement across every durable and private-context surface, retaining only explicitly approved minimal operational metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recent canonical-tracker review and have relevant history across the central session protocol, server, and persisted type surfaces.
